subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Legend of Kaldi
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Legend of Kaldi.

hook.text: An Ethiopian goat herder noticed his goats dancing after eating red berries. He'd found coffee.

buildup.text: Kaldi brought the berries to a monk, who threw them into a fire. The roasting aroma was irresistible.

discovery.text: The monks brewed the roasted beans and stayed awake through evening prayers. Word spread fast.

twist.text: This legend dates to the 9th century but wasn't written down until the 1600s. Its truth is debated.

climax.text: What's certain is that coffee originated in Ethiopia's highland forests, where wild coffee still grows.

punchline.text: Dancing goats, a curious herder, and history changed.

details.summary: The most famous coffee origin story tells of Kaldi, an Ethiopian goat herder who noticed his goats dancing after eating red berries from a certain bush. He brought the berries to a monastery where monks made a drink that kept them alert during prayers. The story is likely apocryphal but enduring.
details.whyItMatters: The Kaldi legend anchors coffee's identity in Ethiopia and illustrates how all great commodities begin with a story of accidental discovery.
takeaways: Kaldi supposedly noticed energized goats eating coffee berries
Monks brewed the berries to stay alert during prayers
The tale is likely myth but places coffee's origin in Ethiopia

faq.question: Is the legend of Kaldi historically accurate?
faq.answer: Almost certainly not. The first written version appears around 1671, centuries after coffee was already widely consumed. No contemporary source mentions Kaldi. The story serves to root coffee in Ethiopia and makes a compelling narrative, but it is folklore rather than history.

faq.question: Where did coffee actually originate?
faq.answer: Coffee arabica evolved in the highland forests of southwestern Ethiopia. The earliest confirmed human consumption was in the Ethiopian-Yemeni region. Exactly when and how people first brewed coffee remains unknown, but Ethiopia is universally recognized as coffee's birthplace.
